case_number: Civil Appeal No. 1269 of 2022 (Arising out of SLP (Civil) No. 20913 of 2018)

parties.respondent: Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation Ltd.

summary: The legal heirs of V. Rajasekaran challenged the High Court's award of Rs.15,12,628/- with 7.5% interest for his death in a motor vehicle accident. The Supreme Court examined the correctness of applying a split multiplier (3 years till retirement and 8 post-retirement). Relying on Sarla Verma and Pranay Sethi, it held that the multiplier must be based on the deceased's age (54 years), not years of service, warranting a multiplier of 11. Future prospects (15%) were added, and compensatory heads recalculated, resulting in enhanced compensation of Rs.24,33,064/- with 9% interest from claim filing. The split multiplier approach was rejected as contrary to binding precedent.
legal_provisions_cited: Sarla Verma (Smt.) & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.
Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr.
National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.
United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur & Ors.
final_judgment: Appeal allowed. Compensation enhanced to Rs.24,33,064/- with 9% interest from the date of filing of claim till realization. Disposed of with costs throughout.
